# @cloudhal/cloudflare

The Cloudhal **admin Worker** (ADR-0012): Studio (static assets), the HTTP API, Better Auth on D1, the MCP endpoint and the push/pull endpoints on one origin, over the deployment's D1 database and R2 bucket. After every publish/rollback it purges the **site Worker**'s edge cache through the `SITE` service binding.

```ts
// worker.ts — generated by `cloudhal deploy`
import "@cloudhal/cloudflare/workerd-prelude"; // must stay first (zod init order, see the module)
import { createAdminWorker } from "@cloudhal/cloudflare/admin";
import skills from "./skills.ts";
export default createAdminWorker({ skills });
```

| Binding / secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DB` (D1), `BLOBS` (R2) | the site graph, snapshots, auth, audit |
| `ASSETS` | built Studio (`not_found_handling: single-page-application`, `run_worker_first` for `/api/*`, `/mcp`, `/.well-known/*`) |
| `SITE` (service) | the site Worker, for cache purges |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `MCP_STATE_KEY` | sessions; signed approval state |
| `CLOUDHAL_PREVIEW_SECRET`, `CLOUDHAL_PURGE_TOKEN` | shared with the site Worker |
| `CLOUDHAL_DEPLOY_TOKEN` | `cloudhal push` / `pull` |
| `CLOUDHAL_SIGNUP` | `first-user` (default — only the first account, the owner, can sign up), `closed` or `open` |

The site Worker itself is the project's Astro build (`@cloudhal/astro-renderer/cloudflare-entry`). Both are deployed, configured and tested by `@cloudhal/cli` (`cloudhal deploy`, `test/cloudflare*.test.ts` on workerd).
